items.item_text: Registered Nurse (RN) license issued by the State of California.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and a pre-employment physical.
A Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Nursing.
A minimum of five (5+) or more years of relevant experience.
Two (2+) or more years of supervisory or management experience.
Previous RN transfer center, ED RN CM or ED RN experience.
Previous experience in UCSD Health Population Health.
Experience supervising union-represented employees.

UC San Diego Health is proud to be a four-time Magnet-designated organization and has now earned Magnet with Distinction from the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). Magnet is the gold standard for nursing excellence, achieved by only about 10% of hospitals worldwide. Magnet with Distinction is awarded to the highest-performing Magnet organizations, with only a select few earning this prestigious honor. This recognition reflects our commitment to transformational leadership, professional nursing excellence, innovation, exceptional patient outcomes, and an empowering practice environment where nurses thrive.

UC San Diego Health is seeking a dynamic and Emergency Department (ED) experienced Registered Nurse (RN) to oversee our innovative Acute Care at Home program under UCSD at Home. This position is housed within UC San Diego Health Population Health Services. This role oversees a small team of RN Transition Care Managers, a Medical Assistant Supervisor, and a team of Medical Assistants who follow patients who can transition out of the ED sooner if they meet criteria. The program functions as a virtual clinic, delivering Tele-Video Visits (TVV) to patients in their homes to promote safe transitions and tight medical management for up to 5 days post-ED discharge. In some instances, the ED to Home program may enroll patients who have had a short inpatient stay but need tighter medical management to mitigate unnecessary, avoidable ED returns. This person works very closely with our Care Connections Hub and UCSD at Home team of geriatric home visiting providers for tight handoffs and referrals between programs, along with our Accent Care Home Health Agency and other partners in the community. The ED MDs perform TVV Sunday–Saturday, helping patients to understand their care and ensure progressive stabilization of the acute condition, and then schedule timely primary care follow-up for ongoing care planning. The Assistant Director works onsite in the ED, alongside the ED and inpatient team to help with early patient identification and care coordination for a safe and timely discharge.
Strong relational skills to help ED team identify, engage and enroll patients in ED to Home using outlined criteria.
Communicate escalations and day-to-day priorities to key stakeholders.
Supports a team of emergency department providers and department staff to ensure metrics are met.
Ensures high-quality, patient-centered care delivery in home settings.
Manages productivity, accountability, and clinical outcomes.
Analyzes data to drive performance and continuous improvement.
Collaborates across departments to build a high-performing program.
RN with strong clinical background and leadership experience.
Prior experience in case management or care coordination, and seen as a go-to resource with leadership qualities.
Proficient in EPIC and data analysis tools.
Solution-focused mindset with the ability to prioritize competing tasks.
Thrives in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Be part of a forward-thinking team transforming care for vulnerable populations. This is an opportunity to lead with purpose, innovate in care delivery, and make a meaningful impact in the lives of seniors.
While not required, a cover letter is highly recommended when applying to this position.
Strong knowledge of discharge planning, transitions of care and clinical disease trajectory.
Knowledge of Epic and UC San Diego Health.
Demonstrated ability to lead process improvement projects across departments, with strong communication and data skills. Ability to create standard work documents and program policies.

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to train and mentor subordinate staff, convey complex clinical and technical information in a clear and concise manner, and prepare and present a variety of reports, documentation, analyses, and project proposals.
